hard.title: How the last Treasury auctions went
lines: 25 Nov 7-Year Note, $44bn: high yield 4.708%, bid-to-cover 2.43 (the 3 before averaged 2.46), indirect bidders took 58% (59% before), dealers took 9%.
24 Nov 1-Year 11-Month FRN (reopening), $28bn: discount margin 0.050%, bid-to-cover 2.87 (the 3 before averaged 2.94), indirect bidders took 61% (66% before), dealers took 39%.
24 Nov 5-Year Note, $70bn: high yield 4.719%, bid-to-cover 2.37 (the 3 before averaged 2.30), indirect bidders took 54% (59% before), dealers took 9%.
23 Nov 2-Year Note, $69bn: high yield 4.700%, bid-to-cover 2.65 (the 3 before averaged 2.61), indirect bidders took 52% (56% before), dealers took 10%.

19 Nov 9-Year 8-Month TIPS (reopening), $19bn: high yield 2.903%, bid-to-cover 2.43 (the 2 before averaged 2.27), indirect bidders took 69% (62% before), dealers took 6%. Stronger demand than the earlier ones.
18 Nov 20-Year Bond, $16bn: high yield 5.459%, bid-to-cover 2.63 (the 3 before averaged 2.61), indirect bidders took 60% (58% before), dealers took 13%.
Bid-to-cover = bids for each dollar sold; indirect bidders are mostly foreign and institutional buyers. Weak demand can lift yields. Context, not a signal.
